engines.name: Macro
engines.credits: Engines from Mutable Instruments Plaits by Emilie Gillet (MIT)

engines.name: Shapes
engines.credits: Macro-oscillator from Mutable Instruments Braids by Emilie Gillet (MIT)

engines.name: Macro Heavy
engines.credits: Heavy engines from Mutable Instruments Plaits by Emilie Gillet (MIT)

engines.name: Six-Op FM
engines.credits: Six-operator FM engine from Mutable Instruments Plaits by Emilie Gillet (MIT); DX7 patch banks as distributed with Plaits

engines.name: FM6
engines.credits: Six-operator FM on msfa, the FM core of Google's music-synthesizer-for-android (Google, Apache-2.0); named after Felucca's FM6 engine (hugelton), both borrowed with thanks; reads DX7 voice data (a Yamaha trademark; not affiliated); built-in voices our own

engines.name: Sophie
engines.credits: Sophie by Matt Estela (github.com/mestela/schwung-sophie, MIT), via the Schwung v2 shim (Schwung plugin ABI by Charles Vestal, MIT)

engines.name: Drums
engines.credits: Kick, tom, snare and hi-hat voices from Mutable Instruments Plaits by Emilie Gillet (MIT); rim, clap, cowbell and cymbal from this repository (MIT), after Werner, Abel and Smith's TR-808 cowbell and cymbal models

engines.name: Acid Bass
engines.credits: A bass after the TB-303: fm1-x0x's 303 by Charles Vestal (GPL-3.0), ported from schwung-303: Open303 by Robin Schmidt (MIT), Devilfish ranges after jc303 by midilab (GPL-3.0), RAT drive after dm-Rat by Dave Mollen (GPL-3.0)

engines.name: Comet Kit
engines.credits: A kit after the TR-909: fm1-x0x's 909 by Charles Vestal (GPL-3.0), ported from 9W9 by athousanddetails (GPL-3.0), which grew out of ER-99 by Matthew Cieplak (GPL-3.0); hi-hat, crash and ride recordings from ER-99 (GPL-3.0)

engines.name: Crater Kit
engines.credits: A kit after the TR-808: fm1-x0x's 808 by Charles Vestal (GPL-3.0), ported from 8W8 by athousanddetails (GPL-3.0): circuit models after the TR-808 service notes and Werner, Abel and Smith; the rim shot after sc808 by Yoshinosuke Horiuchi and Sam Aaron (MIT)

engines.name: Drawbar
engines.credits: Felucca by Leo Kuroshita (@kurogedelic), Hugelton Instruments (GPL-3.0): its WHEEL engine, a tonewheel-style organ of its own design

engines.name: Trio
engines.credits: Felucca by Leo Kuroshita (@kurogedelic), Hugelton Instruments (GPL-3.0): its TRIO engine, three oscillators and a filter in the style of 8-bit sound chips

engines.name: Phase Bend
engines.credits: Felucca by Leo Kuroshita (@kurogedelic), Hugelton Instruments (GPL-3.0): its PHASE engine, a port of the phase-distortion oscillator of CrispyZebra by the same author (GPL-3.0)

engines.name: Test Sine
engines.credits: This repository (MIT)

engines.name: Plate
engines.credits: Reverb from Mutable Instruments Rings by Emilie Gillet (MIT)

engines.name: Ensemble
engines.credits: Ensemble from Mutable Instruments Plaits by Emilie Gillet (MIT)

engines.name: Diffuse
engines.credits: Diffuser from Mutable Instruments Plaits by Emilie Gillet (MIT); tone filter and decorrelator from this repository (MIT)

engines.name: PSX Verb
engines.credits: PSX Verb by Charles Vestal (github.com/charlesvestal/schwung-psxverb, MIT), via the Schwung v2 shim (Schwung plugin ABI by Charles Vestal, MIT)

engines.name: Crush
engines.credits: This repository (MIT); after DaisySP's Decimator and Bitcrush (Electro-Smith, MIT), no code copied

engines.name: Fold
engines.credits: This repository (MIT): a wavefolder after the Serge and Buchla folders and the folding in Mutable Instruments Warps and Plaits (Emilie Gillet), no code taken; anti-aliasing after Parker, Zavalishin and Le Bivic (DAFx-16)

engines.name: Drive
engines.credits: This repository (MIT): overdrive and saturation curves written here; anti-aliasing after Parker, Zavalishin and Le Bivic (DAFx-16)

engines.name: Echo
engines.credits: This repository (MIT). Ping-pong topology after Zoelzer's DAFX; 16-bit delay words after Emilie Gillet's FxEngine (Mutable Instruments, MIT)

engines.name: Warble
engines.credits: Written here (MIT); conceptual inspiration: CHOMPI Warble

engines.name: Filter
engines.credits: This repository (MIT): zero-delay-feedback filters after Zavalishin's The Art of VA Filter Design, Simper's (Cytomic) SVF, Huovilainen's ladder, the Korg35, diode-ladder and Steiner-Parker circuits; vowels from Peterson and Barney (1952). No code taken

engines.name: Comb
engines.credits: This repository (MIT): Zoelzer's universal comb (DAFX, ch. 2), with the Filter's saturating loop. No code taken

engines.name: Comp
engines.credits: This repository (MIT): a feed-forward compressor after Giannoulis, Massberg and Reiss, "Digital Dynamic Range Compressor Design" (JAES 2012); no code taken

engines.name: Limiter
engines.credits: This repository (MIT): a look-ahead limiter after Geraint Luff's "Designing a straightforward limiter" (Signalsmith Audio, 2022), no code taken; Mode Round ports Airwindows ClipOnly2 (Chris Johnson, MIT)

engines.name: DJ Filter
engines.credits: This repository (MIT): a trapezoidal state-variable filter after Andrew Simper (Cytomic) and Vadim Zavalishin, in the form of stmlib's Svf (Emilie Gillet, MIT); no code taken

engines.name: Tilt
engines.credits: This repository (MIT): a tilt equaliser of first-order sections, bilinear and prewarped at the pivot; the idea after Airwindows ToneSlant (MIT) and Faust's spectral_tilt (STK-4.3), no code taken

engines.name: Master Sat
engines.credits: This repository (MIT): band-limited bus saturation; curve coefficients from Airwindows PurestSaturation and TapeHack2 (Chris Johnson, MIT, notice in the source); Glue after Airwindows Compresaturator, no code taken

engines.name: Isolator
engines.credits: This repository (MIT): a three-band kill EQ with Linkwitz-Riley crossovers, the band tree after Faust's crossover3LR4 (filters.lib, STK-4.3), no code taken; TPT state-variable filters after Zavalishin and Simper (Cytomic)

engines.name: EQ
engines.credits: This repository (MIT): low shelf, bell and high shelf on the trapezoidal state-variable filter in the form Andrew Simper (Cytomic) published (public domain), no code taken; tested against the RBJ Audio EQ Cookbook

engines.name: Room
engines.credits: Reverb and diffuser from Mutable Instruments Clouds by Emilie Gillet (MIT); Width and the rate rule from this repository (MIT)

engines.name: Hall
engines.credits: This repository (MIT): a feedback delay network after Jot and Chaigne (1991), structure after schwung-work's Voidspace and Geraint Luff's Signalsmith basics (MIT), no code taken; input all-passes after Schroeder and Dattorro; 16-bit delay words after Emilie Gillet's FxEngine (Mutable Instruments, MIT)

engines.name: Gate
engines.credits: This repository (MIT): a noise gate with controls after the Drawmer DS201 and DS301 manuals; algorithm ours, no code taken

engines.name: Squash
engines.credits: Airwindows (Chris Johnson), MIT: Pop3, Pressure4 and ButterComp2, ported to single precision without libm by this repository (MIT)

engines.name: Transient
engines.credits: This repository (MIT): a transient shaper on the differential-envelope principle (a fast and a slow follower), our own arithmetic; no code taken

engines.name: Test Gain
engines.credits: This repository (MIT)

engines.name: Test Ext
engines.credits: This repository (MIT)

engines.name: Arp
engines.credits: Lunar Modulator's arpeggiator (MIT): after Yarns' arpeggiator by Emilie Gillet (MIT), MCL's note orders by Justin Mammarella (BSD-3) and Super Arp's modifiers by Handcrafted Media (MIT); reimplemented, engines/midi_fx/CREDITS.md

engines.name: Acid Gen
engines.credits: Acid lines from TB-3PO, the generator in fm1-x0x by Charles Vestal (GPL-3.0), after schwung-tb3po and the Phazerville Hemisphere Suite's TB_3PO applet by djphazer and contributors (GPL-3.0)

kinds.name: LFO
kinds.credits: Our own, on fm1_mp's LFO. Shapes after Schwung's lfo_common.h (Charles Vestal, MIT) and Mutable Instruments' Peaks (Emilie Gillet, MIT); modes after Elektron's.

kinds.name: Envelope
kinds.credits: Our own, on fm1_mp's multistage envelope after Mutable Instruments' Peaks (Emilie Gillet, MIT): its segments, presets, curves and knob-to-time curve.

kinds.name: Chance
kinds.credits: Our own, on fm1_mp's LFO, slew and generator. After DaisySP's SampleHold (Electrosmith, Paul Batchelor, MIT) and Music Thing Modular Workshop System Computer card 106 (Matt Allison, MIT).

kinds.name: Function
kinds.credits: Our own, from the published behaviour of Make Noise's Maths, Joranalogue's Contour 1, Serge's DUSG and Befaco's Rampage; shape curves after Mutable Instruments' Peaks (Emilie Gillet, MIT).

kinds.name: Bounce
kinds.credits: Ported from Mutable Instruments' Peaks bouncing ball (Emilie Gillet, MIT), byte-identical at its 48 kHz rate; the HIT output is ours.

kinds.name: Register
kinds.credits: Our own, on fm1_mp's register. After Music Thing Modular's Turing Machine (Tom Whitwell), Workshop System Computer card 20 (Chris Johnson, MIT) and Phazerville's util_turing.h (Patrick Dowling, MIT); no code taken.

kinds.name: Coin
kinds.credits: Our own, from the published behaviour of Mutable Instruments' Branches (GPL-3 firmware, not read). MIT references: Marbles' coin toss and Phazerville's Brancher.

kinds.name: Divide
kinds.credits: Our own. After Phazerville's ClockDivider, ProbabilityDivider, Shuffle and GateDelay and Piqued's Euclidean filter (Jason Justian, Nicholas J. Michalek and others, MIT); no code taken.

kinds.name: Burst
kinds.credits: Ported from Mutable Instruments' Peaks pulse shaper and pulse randomizer (Emilie Gillet, MIT), byte-identical; Accel and the clocked spacing are ours. After Phazerville's Burst (Jason Justian, MIT; no code taken).

kinds.name: Slew
kinds.credits: Our own. After the disting mk4's slew (Expert Sleepers; idea only), Phazerville's Slew (MIT) and Just Friends' STRATA (Mannequins; idea only); no code taken.

kinds.name: Quantize
kinds.credits: Ported from Mutable Instruments' Braids quantizer and its scales (Emilie Gillet, MIT), byte-identical; as Phazerville's Quantermain uses it.

kinds.name: Compare
kinds.credits: Our own. After Phazerville's Compare, Schmitt and Trending (Jason Justian, MIT), Chris Johnson's Utility Pair window comparator (MIT) and the disting mk4's comparator (Expert Sleepers; idea only); no code taken.

kinds.name: Logic
kinds.credits: Our own. After Phazerville's Logic and TL Neuron (Jason Justian, MIT) and the disting NT's Logic (Expert Sleepers; idea only); no code taken.

kinds.name: Calc
kinds.credits: Our own. After Mutable Instruments' Kinks and Links (analog), Phazerville's Calculate (Jason Justian, MIT) and Music Thing Modular Workshop System Computer card 107 (Matt Allison, MIT); no code taken.

kinds.name: Mix
kinds.credits: Our own. After Mutable Instruments' Links and Shades (analog) and Phazerville's AttenuateOffset and Combin8 (MIT); no code taken.

kinds.name: Resonator
kinds.credits: Our own: the trapezoidal state-variable filter after Andrew Simper's (Cytomic) published derivation, at the control rate.
